[Chunk 1 | chunk_id=06cb24ff-a7ef-4959-9438-9b7c189209bc | doc_id=arxiv:2608.12493 | title=Beyond the Skew-Stickiness Ratio: Transport Geometry of Spot-Driven Variance Surface Dynamics | uri=https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12493 | section=General Transport Fields and the Smile Jet Hierarchy > Interpretation]
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
The generalized transport theory replaces the single SSR parameter by a local
transport velocity field. Skew dynamics are governed by its first derivative at ATM, curvature dynamics by
its second derivative, and higher-order smile dynamics by higher derivatives.
This gives a natural extension of the SSR. Rather than postulating separate
parameters for level, skew and curvature, the theory identifies them as the ATM
jet of the velocity field itself:

$v(0),\ \partial_k v(0),\ \partial_k^2 v(0),\ldots$

The general case yields a nonlinear
characteristic flow and a corresponding generalized ride formula. The remaining
question is which transport velocity fields preserve static arbitrage. This is
the subject of the next section.
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

[Chunk 2 | chunk_id=048f7f8e-9848-481c-aa61-9d5e547f6e37 | doc_id=arxiv:2608.12493 | title=Beyond the Skew-Stickiness Ratio: Transport Geometry of Spot-Driven Variance Surface Dynamics | uri=https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12493 | section=Empirical Evidence from SPX > Experiment 5: Transport or Source?]
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
Proposition~Proposition identification-without-inversion makes the
pure-transport hypothesis testable without dividing by anything. This
experiment reuses the SPX implied-volatility surface data of
Experiments 1--4, restricted to the

$797$

dates admitting a stable
local-cubic skew fit at each node. The regressions are run on first
differences, so they use those increments whose two endpoints are both
available and consecutive in the filtered panel; the realized count is
reported per tenor in Table~Table pure-transport-fixed and is smaller
than

$797$

for that reason. We use the tenor forward as the regressor

$\Delta u=\Delta\log F(T)$

, the daily skew

$b_1(k_0,t)$

from a local
cubic fit (half-width 5 nodes) re-gridded onto 41 log-moneyness nodes,
and Newey--West standard errors with 5 lags. The quoted strike range
covers roughly

$85$

--

$115\%$

of spot; at 1M and 3M this comfortably
contains the interior smile minimum on most trading days, but by 6M and
1Y the minimum has migrated outside it (Remark~Rem inversion-fails),
so the minimum-based tests below are run at 1M and 3M only. The
at-the-money test does not require the minimum to be in range and is
reported at all four tenors.

\textbf{The fixed-node test.} We fit Equation identification-vs node by
node and test

$H_0:s=0$

at two places: at the money, where

$|b_1|$

is large
and the diagnostics of Experiments 1--3 are computed, and, at 1M and 3M,
at the node nearest the minimum of the sample-mean smile, where

$\mathcal T_w$

is n

[Chunk 3 | chunk_id=0754feba-a828-49cc-9211-7e11d76ffe5f | doc_id=arxiv:2608.12493 | title=Beyond the Skew-Stickiness Ratio: Transport Geometry of Spot-Driven Variance Surface Dynamics | uri=https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12493 | section=Extensions > Term-Structure Transport]
The estimated coefficients have a non-trivial term structure:

$\hat\beta$

decays monotonically,

$\hat\eta$

crosses zero between 6M and 9M, and

$\hat\zeta$

decays toward zero (Table~Table jet-sequential). Here that
maturity dependence is accommodated by letting

$v=v(k,T)$

and estimating at
each tenor independently; the dynamics in the maturity direction are not
modeled. The transport equation moves the surface in

$k$

only, with

$T$

held
fixed along each characteristic. Allowing

$T$

to evolve replaces the velocity
by a pair

$(v,\lambda)$

,

\[
 \dot k_\tau = -v(k_\tau,T_\tau),
 \qquad
 \dot T_\tau = -\lambda(k_\tau,T_\tau),
 \qquad
 \partial_u w = v\,\partial_k w + \lambda\,\partial_T w,
\]

for which a

$T$

-affine ansatz

$v=\gamma_0+\gamma_1 T$

would capture the
observed maturity dependence; this is the implied-variance counterpart of the
term-structure program of Schweizer and Wissel~\cite{SchweizerWissel2008} and
the tangent-model formulation of Carmona and
Nadtochiy~\cite{CarmonaNadtochiy2011}. Establishing admissibility for the
coupled field is harder than the problem solved in
Section~Section arb-preservation, because

$\lambda$

enters the
calendar-density equation~Equation q-transport directly, so calendar and
butterfly preservation must be established jointly under the two-dimensional
flow. Compatibility of local jet representations centered at different
strikes is likewise not addressed here.
